These notes introduce differential calculus: limits, continuity, derivatives, and their applications. They grow alongside the lectures, with explanations, graphs, and worked examples organized by topic.

[See the latest class](lectures/08-exam-practice.qmd){.start-link}

**October 5:** Limits and continuity — exam practice.

New here? [Begin with Chapter 1](lectures/01-introduction.qmd).

Read the numbered chapters in order, or use the contents and search to return to a particular idea.

For the original handouts, visit the [lecture PDF archive](lecture-pdfs.qmd), organized by date.

The [precalculus review](lectures/00-functions.qmd) is **Appendix A**, with its original [review PDF](downloads/september-25-chapter-1-review.pdf).

## References

These notes draw on the exposition, examples, and ideas in the following texts, adapted to the sequence and emphasis of this course:

- Gilbert Strang and Edwin “Jed” Herman, [*Calculus Volume 1*](https://openstax.org/details/books/calculus-volume-1). OpenStax.
- James Stewart, [*Calculus*](https://www.stewartcalculus.com/). Cengage.
- Michael Spivak, [*Calculus*](https://mathpop.com/products/calculus-4th-edition-digital-edition). Publish or Perish.
